_doc: Example .factory/profile.json — a Python API service. Copy to .factory/profile.json in your repo and replace every value. Validate against templates/profile.schema.json. Everything here is a real, checkable fact about the repo: no aspirations, no 'should'. If a role gets something wrong twice, the fix belongs in this file.
estate_role: Owns the HTTP contract and the database schema; acme-web and acme-worker consume it. Cross-repo epics are filed here.
stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI + Uvicorn, Pydantic v2, PostgreSQL 16, SQLAlchemy Core, Alembic, Docker
conventions: Data access lives in store/{domain}_store.py — parameterised SQL only, never string interpolation
Routes in api/routes_{domain}.py; register the router in main.py under the /api prefix
Every endpoint declares its auth dependency explicitly — there is no permissive default
Request/response models are Pydantic v2 classes in schemas/{domain}.py, never bare dicts
Timestamps are stored UTC and converted at the edge, never in the store layer
review_checklist: Authorization present on every new or changed endpoint
Parameterised SQL only — no f-string or %-format SQL anywhere in the diff
New tables/columns have an Alembic migration, and it downgrades cleanly
No secrets in code or logs; config only through the existing env-var mechanism
Pagination on any endpoint that can return an unbounded collection
qa_notes: Tests live in tests/test_{domain}.py with the store layer monkeypatched — no database needed
Migration tests run against a disposable Postgres via docker compose -f compose.test.yml
Where design.md calls for it, drive the running container rather than the app object
gotchas: tests/test_legacy_import.py fails on a clean checkout — pre-existing, not your delta
Never source .env in a test command; it overrides the CI database URL
ruff is configured with a narrow rule set on purpose — do not widen it to fix a finding

notes: The container entrypoint runs `alembic upgrade head` and exits non-zero on failure — a red deploy means the schema did not migrate. Halt the train; do not merge downstream consumers.
